abilities.name: Precision Hydronic Cooler

_curatorNotes: The DEFAULT cadence. gcsim asc.go a1BurstEnhance returns (90f, radius 1, ICDGroupDefault) below Ascension 1 or Moonsign level 2; burst.go loops `for i := 0; i < 14.2*60; i += tickrate` scheduling each tick at `i + burstStart`.

firstTickDelay 0.167 is the TEN FRAMES of travel on every tick — gcsim queues each one with `QueueAttack(ai, ..., 0, 10)`, so the whole series lands 10f after it fires. ⚠️ It shifts the series rather than just the first tick, which is what a constant travel offset is. Before this the audit read authored 123f against observed 133f on every tick.
icdGate ABSENT = the standard window, which IS gcsim’s Default group here — ⛔ do not annotate it (icd.md forbids restating the default). Measured 5/10 applied.

effects.attribution: A1: Modular Efficiency Protocol (Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam)
_curatorNotes: ⚓⚓ THE ASCENDANT GLEAM CADENCE. gcsim asc.go a1BurstEnhance: at Ascension ≥ 1 AND GetMoonsignLevel() ≥ 2 the burst’s tickrate becomes 0.7*60 = 42f (from 90f), the radius 1 → 4, and the ICD group becomes ICDGroupAinoBurstMoonHit. ⚠️ It is not only a faster interval — all three change together, which is why this is a SECOND series rather than an interval override.

icdGate is ICDGroupAinoBurstMoonHit verbatim: 108f reset window, every 4th hit applies (pkg/core/attacks/icd_groups.dm.go:74,135). ⛔ Not the standard, and at a 42f interval the two are very different — the whole reason the group changes with the rate.

tickCap 21: gcsim’s loop bound is `i < 14.2*60` in steps of 42, i.e. 21 ticks, while the summon’s authored lifetime is 14s and our half-open walk over it yields 20. The cap is how the boundary tick is said — see the tickCap schema note.

⚠️⚠️ THE ORACLE CANNOT SEE THIS BRANCH. `scripts/gcsim-dump` runs one character in an empty core, where Aino’s own Moonsign is 1 and GetMoonsignLevel() < 2 — so the dump always measures the DEFAULT series and a green frames-diff proves nothing about this one. Authored from the Go, like `chargedIcdWindow` was.

⚓ This is what the A1 passive’s curator note asked for: it recorded the enhanced rate as unauthorable because "teamFaction conditions on summon-effect triggers don’t currently resolve at parse time". They do now — `finalize` is the one producer for a summon’s markers and it builds the condition context.

_curatorNotes: Cool Your Jets Ducky: stationary turret summoned at burstStart=123f from cast, 14s duration. Fires a water ball every 1.5s base (0.7s w/ Moonsign Gleam via a1BurstEnhance). Per-tick: burst[lvl=10]=36.20% ATK Hydro + a4Dmg=50%×EM (Aino's EM) FlatDmg.
Authored as summons[] entry with summonTick effect at 1.5s interval. firstTickDelay=0 since the loop starts immediately after spawn (i=0 first tick at burstStart+0).
Burst frames: burstFrames=InitAbilSlice(60), ActionAttack/Charge/Skill=55 ActionDash/Jump=56 ActionSwap=54. Per Q-spec swap/N/E/D/J.
Cooldown: SetCD(burst, 13.5*60). Note: cooldown 13.5 < duration 14 — the planner will render Phase 2 (dim continuation) for the last 0.5s of the active duration after CD resets.
ConsumeEnergy(5) drains 5 energy from teammates; not modelled.
EnergyMax=50 (matches energyCost). C2 trigger (off-field active hits) and C6 reaction-DMG bonus are deferred — see constellation entries.

[A7] Caveat previously also stated the summon's AoE radius increases under Moonsign Ascendant Gleam (1 → 4); dropped from the user-facing caveat because the timeline does not display AoE radius, so it is not a divergence the user could be misled by. The radius change is already documented in the A1 passive (Modular Efficiency Protocol) curator note.

constellations.name: The Theory of Ash—Field Equilibrium
_curatorNotes: C1: on E or Q cast, +80 EM to Aino self AND +80 EM to team for 15s. gcsim c1Init applies the buff on c1OnSkillBurst (called from both Skill and Burst). Authored as two separate effects with onCast trigger and no `ability` field — fires for both skill and burst per curation convention. duration:15 matches the c1Key status.
Description says 'effects do not stack' — both buffs share a 15s window but neither overrides the other on re-cast. Schema's durationType:fixed handles this acceptably.
constellations.description:
After Aino uses her Elemental Skill **Musecatcher** or her Elemental Burst **Precision Hydronic Cooler**, her Elemental Mastery will be increased by 80. The Elemental Mastery of other nearby active party members will be increased by 80 for 15s.

constellations.name: The Principle of Transference in Gear Differentials
_curatorNotes: C2: when Aino is off-field AND the burst is active AND the active character hits an enemy, fire a 25% ATK + 100% EM Hydro hit on a 5s ICD. gcsim cons.go c2Init subscribes to OnEnemyHit gated on burstKey active + Aino off-field + c2IcdKey 5*60, landing 10f later (QueueAttack(..., 0, 10)).

↻ AUTHORED 2026-08-18. The three primitives its old note deferred all exist now: an `onHit` damage effect carrying an `application[]` is read by `sim/procs.ts` (coordinated-attack round), `source: "others"` is the off-field half, and hosting it on the burst’s summon makes the summon’s own liveness the "burst is active" window — so no `armedFor` and no `duringSummon` state are needed.

⚠️ `source: "others"` is one step wider than gcsim in exactly one place: gcsim also requires the hitter to BE the active character, and an off-field summon owned by a third party carries its owner’s id, so its ticks reach this where gcsim’s would not. `onHit` has no `"active"` source, and the mark-triggered round records why an id test alone cannot supply one.

FlatDmg is `em + a4Dmg()` in gcsim — the C2’s own 100% EM plus A4 Structured Power Booster’s +50% of EM on Elemental Burst DMG, which this hit counts as. Hence flatScaling 150, against the base tick’s 50 (A4 alone).
icdGate "none" is gcsim’s ICDTagNone on the C2 attack: every projection applies its full 1U Hydro, unlike the burst’s own ticks.

⚠️ THE EFFECT LIVES ON THE BURST’S SUMMON, not here — `aino__burst__precision_hydronic_cooler` → "Cool Your Jets Ducky" → effects[]. That is where the WINDOW is: gcsim gates the proc on `burstKey`, which is the same 14s the summon holds, so hosting it there makes the summon’s own liveness the arming window (no `armedFor`, and swap/recast truncation for free). ⚓ Same arrangement Fischl’s A4 uses on Oz. It also draws its markers on the duck’s lane, which is what the kit text describes: "the Cool Your Jets Ducky will fire an additional water ball".
constellations.description: If Aino is off-field while the Focused Hydronic Cooling Zone of her Elemental Burst **Precision Hydronic Cooler** is active, when your active party member hits a nearby opponent with an attack, the Cool Your Jets Ducky will fire an additional water ball at that opponent, dealing AoE Hydro DMG equal to 25% of Aino's ATK and 100% of her Elemental Mastery. This DMG is considered Elemental Burst DMG. This effect can be triggered once every 5s.

constellations.name: The Burden of Creative Genius
_curatorNotes: COMPLETE 2026-07-29: all 5 reactions authored. The wiki files this constellation under the five '<Reaction> DMG Bonus' categories = the bucket-5 Reaction Bonus bracket, so every effect was RE-KEYED from lunar*DmgBonus to the *ReactionBonus stat family (Nate's bucket-5 ruling), and the long-deferred Electro-Charged + Bloom pair landed on electroChargedReactionBonus / bloomReactionBonus with the same two-tier Gleam shape.

Two-tier authoring: each of the 3 Lunar stats has TWO mutually-exclusive effects. When ≥2 Moonsign units (Ascendant Gleam active) → +35% (15 base + 20 Gleam, baked together). When <2 → +15% only. The renderer's per-stat de-dup picks the first matching effect, so the Gleam-active effects are listed first; if the teamFaction condition fails, evalCondition returns false and the renderer falls through to the non-Gleam tier. Conditions are mutually exclusive (`teamFaction min:2` vs `not(teamFaction min:2)`) so exactly one tier ever applies.

Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam: DMG from the aforementioned reactions will be further increased by 20%.
